title: FinCEN Assesses Historic $80 Million Penalty Against Canaccord Genuity LLC for Securities Fraud-Related Bank Secrecy Act Violations
summary: On 6 March 2026, FinCEN assessed an $80,000,000 civil money penalty against Canaccord Genuity LLC, a broker-dealer FinCEN's release describes as acting in a market-making capacity, for willful violations of the Bank Secrecy Act. FinCEN's release states Canaccord failed to develop and maintain an effective anti-money-laundering program with adequate risk-based customer due diligence, failed to establish internal controls to monitor transactions for suspicious activity, failed to file at least 160 suspicious activity reports tied to dozens of over-the-counter securities fraud schemes -- including penny-stock and microcap fraud -- and failed to conduct due diligence on foreign correspondent accounts. FinCEN states this is the largest penalty it has ever imposed on a broker-dealer for BSA violations, reached with cooperation from the SEC and FINRA.
why_it_matters: FinCEN's release does not mention digital assets, crypto, or virtual currency -- this action concerns a traditional broker-dealer's securities-fraud-related Bank Secrecy Act failures, unconnected to crypto or digital assets. It is included here because FinCEN describes it as the largest BSA penalty it has ever imposed on a broker-dealer, applying the same Bank Secrecy Act program-adequacy and reporting standards this pillar otherwise tracks for money-services businesses that handle convertible virtual currency.

citations.quote: This is the largest penalty ever imposed against a broker-dealer for violating the BSA.
